entries.description: Use whenever the user unloads a messy brain dump of ideas, tasks and plans ('capture this', 'brain dump', a long unstructured paste) and wants it organized. Sorts it with dump_classifier.py into projects, tasks and connections with nothing lost.

entries.name: deep-work
entries.description: Use when someone wants to plan a deep work day, time-block their calendar or task list, budget or cut shallow work, protect focus hours, track deep-work sessions and streaks, run an end-of-day shutdown ritual, or says "/deep-work" or "/time-block". Classifies tasks deep vs shallow, builds an energy-first time-blocked schedule that refuses deep demand past the 4-hour ceiling, batches shallow work into at most two windows, and logs focus sessions against a weekly target.

entries.name: inbox-setup
entries.description: Use when setting up email triage for the first time, before inbox-triage, or when priorities change. Interviews the user one question at a time and writes the knowledge base inbox-triage reads, validated with kb_validator.py.

entries.name: inbox-triage
entries.description: Use when the user wants their inbox processed ('triage my inbox', 'check my email'). Classifies recent mail with the inbox-setup knowledge base, drafts replies it never sends (checked by draft_safety_validator.py) and reports.

entries.name: fable-goal
entries.description: Use when the user wants a /goal prompt rather than the build itself ('/fable-goal', 'turn this into a goal prompt', 'write the prompt that builds X'). Turns their ramble into one copy-paste prompt checked by goal_prompt_self_check.py.

entries.name: session-handoff
entries.description: Write a handoff document so a fresh session or another agent can pick up exactly where this one left off: goal, current state, decisions, next steps and the skills to load, referencing existing files instead of copying them, with secrets redacted before saving. Use whenever the user is ending a session, switching machines, running low on context, or asks for a handoff, a handoff doc, a 'pick up where we left off' summary, or to compact the conversation for next time. Saves to a location the user picks on first run (OS temp, home folder or per-project .handoff/) and can auto-load the latest handoff at the next session start.

entries.name: meetings
entries.description: Use when someone wants to decide whether a meeting is worth calling, price a meeting in dollars, build a timeboxed agenda with desired outcomes, or turn messy meeting notes into owned action items — or says "should this be a meeting", "/cs-meeting-prep", or "/cs-meeting-actions". Runs a cost gate (ASYNC / NOT-READY / MEET), builds a decision-first agenda, and extracts an owner + due-date checklist that flags every orphan.

entries.name: monetize
entries.description: Use when someone asks how to earn more from their own experience: side income, side hustle, monetizing a skill, salary ceiling, career leverage, 副业, 变现, 外快, 技能变现, 薪资天花板, or pastes a résumé asking what they could do with it. Builds one person's side-income plan (hidden-skills audit, opportunity scan, productization, one leverage action, salary ceiling, AI starter pack) with every number sourced or labeled, and lints the report with report_lint.py.

entries.name: reflect
entries.description: Use when the user says 'step back', 'zoom out', 'are we on track' or 'sanity check this', or work has gone deep into details without a check on direction. Reassesses direction, assumptions and bias across five dimensions.

entries.name: roast
entries.description: Roast an idea: a 5-angle panel (Critic, Champion, Analyst, Investigator, Customer) attacks it, then a Judge returns one GO / RESHAPE / KILL verdict with the cheapest test to de-risk it. Use whenever the user wants to pressure-test or validate a business idea, asks for a brutal second opinion before building, asks is this a good idea, says convene the panel, or runs /roast.

entries.name: swedish-mentor
entries.description: Use when someone learning Swedish wants a learning path or YouTube clips and podcasts matched to their CEFR level and skill (SFI, Lätt Svenska, Radio Sweden på lätt svenska).

entries.name: weekly-review
entries.description: Use when someone wants to run a weekly review, close open loops, audit stalled projects and commitments, get their system back to trusted, restart a lapsed review habit, or says "/cs-weekly-review". Walks David Allen's three-phase loop — GET CLEAR, GET CURRENT, GET CREATIVE — with deterministic scripts that inventory open loops, gate the checklist with named gaps, and score commitment health 0-100.

entries.name: atlassian-admin
entries.description: Use for Atlassian org administration: Jira or Confluence users and groups, permissions, SSO, marketplace apps or security policy. Audits permissions with permission_audit_tool.py.

entries.name: atlassian-templates
entries.description: Use when creating or changing Jira or Confluence templates, blueprints or page layouts for reuse across the org. Scaffolds them with template_scaffolder.py.

entries.name: confluence-expert
entries.description: Use when building or restructuring a Confluence space: page hierarchy, permissions, templates, Jira macros or a content audit. Generates structure with space_structure_generator.py and audits with content_audit_analyzer.py.

entries.name: jira-expert
entries.description: Jira setup and queries: JQL, workflows, custom fields, automation, dashboards. Use whenever the user needs a Jira search, filter, dashboard or rule set up, or a workflow fixed.

entries.name: meeting-analyzer
entries.description: Use when the user shares meeting transcripts (.vtt, .srt, .txt, Otter, Granola, Zoom) or asks how they come across in meetings. Measures speaking ratio, filler words and avoidance patterns and gives coaching.

entries.name: pm-skills
entries.description: Router for project-management skills: sprints, portfolio health, Jira, Confluence, stakeholder comms, plus a delivery loop. Use whenever a delivery request is unclear about which PM skill fits, or the user asks to run a delivery loop or pull Jira data into one.

entries.name: scrum-master
entries.description: Use for sprint and team analytics: velocity forecasts, sprint health, retrospectives, burndown or blockers. Forecasts with velocity_analyzer.py (Monte Carlo), scores with sprint_health_scorer.py and tracks retro actions with retrospective_analyzer.py.

entries.name: senior-pm
entries.description: Project and portfolio management for multi-workstream programs: plans, status reports, risk registers, capacity, executive reporting. Use whenever the user asks how a project is tracking, what the risks are or who has capacity.

entries.name: team-communications
entries.description: Use for any internal communication: 3P updates, weekly or status reports, newsletters, FAQs, incident reports, leadership updates ('write my update'). Drafts it in the right format for the audience.

entries.name: access-lifecycle
entries.description: Use when preparing or running a user access review, checking that leavers lost their access, finding orphaned or ownerless service accounts, answering an auditor's access-control request for SOC 2, ISO 27001, PCI DSS, HIPAA or NIST 800-53, or checking whether a finished review campaign will hold up. Diffs the HR roster against account exports, tests the campaign for coverage, self-review, unremoved revokes and rubber-stamping, and maps every exception to the controls it breaks.

entries.name: cmmc-readiness
entries.description: Use when a defense contractor or subcontractor is preparing for a CMMC 2.0 Level 2 self-assessment or C3PAO assessment, calculating or checking an SPRS score against NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2, deciding what can go on a POA&M, tracking POA&M closeout before Conditional status expires, or scoping assets, enclaves and cloud providers that handle CUI. Scores all 110 requirements with the 32 CFR 170.24 weights, blocks gaps that can never be deferred, and classifies the asset inventory into CMMC asset categories.

entries.name: eu-ai-act-specialist
entries.description: Use for EU AI Act (Regulation 2024/1689) compliance work: classifying an AI system's risk tier, planning the Art. 43 conformity route and Annex IV file, or listing obligations by role. Runs ai_system_risk_classifier.py, conformity_assessment_planner.py and ai_act_obligation_tracker.py, citing Articles.

entries.name: iso42001-specialist
entries.description: Use for ISO/IEC 42001 AI management system work: gap analysis against Clauses 4-10, the AI risk register and Annex A controls, or the internal audit plan. Runs aims_gap_analyzer.py, ai_risk_register_builder.py and aims_audit_scheduler.py.

entries.name: cra-readiness
entries.description: Use when a company that sells software, connected devices or firmware in the EU asks whether the Cyber Resilience Act (CRA, Regulation 2024/2847) applies, has to report an actively exploited vulnerability or security incident under Article 14 (24h/72h deadlines, ENISA Single Reporting Platform), must classify products as important or critical, pick a conformity route or support period, check an SBOM, or get to CE marking by December 2027. Four deterministic scripts with cited articles.

entries.name: dora-readiness
entries.description: Use when a bank, payment or e-money institution, investment firm, insurer, crypto-asset service provider or fund manager in the EU faces DORA (Regulation 2022/2554, Digital Operational Resilience Act) - is an ICT outage or cyber incident major, when the initial (4h/24h), intermediate (72h) and final reports are due, weekends included; the register of information; ICT or cloud contracts missing audit rights, exit plans or other Article 30 terms; scope and the simplified framework for small firms. Not for DORA DevOps metrics. Three deterministic scripts with cited articles.

entries.name: medical-device-software
entries.description: Use for any question about the software inside a medical device, SaMD or regulated health app - which IEC 62304 safety class (A/B/C) it is and how much process and documentation that class needs, what to record about open-source or third-party libraries (SOUP, SBOM), trace matrix and release testing, IEC 81001-5-1 security, or the FDA documentation level and 524B cyber-device duties. Checks the user's files with four scripts that cite the clause.

entries.name: nis2-readiness
entries.description: Use when a cyberattack, ransomware or outage hits a hospital, utility, transport, digital-infrastructure or other EU company and it must report under NIS2 (Directive 2022/2555) or the German NIS2UmsuCG/BSIG - 24h early warning, 72h notification, one-month final report. Also for whether a company is an essential or important entity, BSI registration, management-board liability and training (Article 20), an Article 21 gap analysis, or one incident that also triggers DORA, CRA or GDPR reports. Four deterministic scripts with cited articles.

entries.name: agent-decision-receipts

entries.name: capa-officer
entries.description: Use for CAPA work in a medical device QMS: root cause analysis (5-Why, fishbone), corrective action plans, effectiveness checks or CAPA metrics. Tracks CAPAs with capa_tracker.py and analyzes causes with root_cause_analyzer.py.

entries.name: fda-consultant-specialist
entries.description: Use for FDA medical device questions: 510(k) vs De Novo vs PMA, predicates and substantial equivalence, QMSR (21 CFR 820), HIPAA or device cybersecurity. Runs fda_submission_tracker.py, qsr_compliance_checker.py and hipaa_risk_assessment.py.

entries.name: gdpr-dsgvo-expert
entries.description: Use for GDPR or DSGVO work: scanning a codebase for privacy risks, writing a DPIA or tracking data subject requests against the Art. 12(3) deadline. Runs gdpr_compliance_checker.py, dpia_generator.py and data_subject_rights_tracker.py; final calls go to the DPO.

entries.name: information-security-manager-iso27001
entries.description: Use when designing or running an ISO 27001 ISMS in HealthTech or MedTech: risk assessment, control implementation, certification or security incidents. Assesses risk with risk_assessment.py and checks controls with compliance_checker.py.

entries.name: isms-audit-expert
entries.description: Use for ISO 27001 audit work: internal or surveillance audits, Annex A control evidence, Statement of Applicability, nonconformities, Stage 1 and 2 prep. Plans risk-based audits with isms_audit_scheduler.py.

entries.name: iso42001-specialist
entries.description: Use for ISO/IEC 42001 AI management system work: gap analysis against Clauses 4-10, the AI risk register and Annex A controls, or the internal audit plan. Runs aims_gap_analyzer.py, ai_risk_register_builder.py and aims_audit_scheduler.py.

entries.name: mdr-745-specialist
entries.description: Use for EU MDR 2017/745 work: device classification under Annex VIII, technical file gaps (Annex II/III), clinical evaluation, PMS and PSUR cadence, notified body prep. Checks the file with mdr_gap_analyzer.py.

entries.name: qms-audit-expert
entries.description: Use for ISO 13485 internal audits: planning the program, running an audit, classifying findings or preparing for an external audit. Optimizes the schedule with audit_schedule_optimizer.py.

entries.name: quality-documentation-manager
entries.description: Use for QMS document control: numbering, versioning, change control or 21 CFR Part 11 e-signatures. Validates documents with document_validator.py and tracks versions with document_version_control.py.

entries.name: quality-manager-qmr
entries.description: Use for QMR duties under ISO 13485 5.5.2: management review, quality policy and objectives, quality KPIs and cost of quality. Tracks reviews with management_review_tracker.py and monitors effectiveness with quality_effectiveness_monitor.py.

entries.name: quality-manager-qms-iso13485
entries.description: Build or maintain an ISO 13485 medical device QMS: design, documentation, CAPA, audit prep. Use whenever the user faces a 13485 certification audit or needs quality procedures.

entries.name: ra-qm-skills
entries.description: Router for regulatory and quality skills: ISO 13485, MDR, FDA, ISO 14971, CAPA, ISO 27001, ISO 42001, EU AI Act, GDPR, SOC 2. Use whenever a compliance request fits no single one.

entries.name: regulatory-affairs-head
entries.description: Use for medical device market access strategy: FDA 510(k), De Novo or PMA packages, CE marking under MDR, pre-sub meetings, agency deficiency responses or multi-market plans. Analyzes pathways with regulatory_pathway_analyzer.py and tracks submissions with regulatory_tracker.py.

entries.name: risk-management-specialist
entries.description: Use for ISO 14971 medical device risk management: hazard analysis, FMEA, fault trees, risk controls, benefit-risk or residual risk. Runs fmea_analyzer.py and risk_matrix_calculator.py.

entries.name: soc2-compliance
entries.description: Use when the user asks to prepare for SOC 2 audits, map Trust Service Criteria, build control matrices, collect audit evidence, perform gap analysis, or assess SOC 2 Type I vs Type II readiness.

entries.name: clinical-research
entries.description: Use when designing a prospective clinical study: choosing primary and secondary endpoints, estimating sample size and power, or scoring feasibility before submission. Runs endpoint_selector.py, sample_size_estimator.py and phase_gate_scorer.py; outputs are estimates for a biostatistician to confirm.

entries.name: interview-mapper
entries.description: Use when coding or making sense of one interview transcript (customer, JTBD, expert, usability, exit). Extracts verbatim-grounded nuggets with extract_nuggets.py, verifies quotes with verify_quotes.py and checks conclusions hold across reruns with consensus.py.

entries.name: market-research
entries.description: Use for market sizing (TAM, SAM, SOM both top-down and bottom-up), survey sample sizes or segment scoring. Runs market_sizer.py, sample_size_planner.py and segmentation_scorer.py and never returns one unsourced number.

entries.name: product-research
entries.description: Use when planning or synthesizing user research: choosing the method, deciding how many participants, or turning coded notes into insights. Runs study_designer.py, saturation_planner.py and insight_synthesizer.py, which refuses single-source insights.

entries.name: research-finance
entries.description: Use for R&D program money: multi-period budgets with indirect cost split, burn and runway against milestones, or capitalize vs expense routing. Runs program_budget_planner.py, burn_runway_tracker.py and capex_vs_opex_router.py.

entries.name: research-ops-skills
entries.description: Use when an enterprise research request needs routing (clinical study design, R&D finance, market sizing, user research): 'what sample size', 'R&D budget'. Lists the research-ops skills and routes to one.

entries.name: deepread
entries.description: Use when the user asks to deeply read a book, article, PDF, or document set; extract claims and evidence; build a knowledge map; or learn through Feynman explanation and recall. Covers quick, deep, map, Feynman, and whole-book reading modes.

entries.name: dossier
entries.description: Use for diligence or meeting prep on a specific company, person or organization ('prep me for a meeting with X', 'due diligence on Y'). Tests the user's stated hypothesis with balanced evidence (disconfirming_evidence_balance.py) and writes a .docx dossier.

entries.name: grants
entries.description: Use for any NIH funding question ('find grants for my research', 'which NIH institute'). Maps the idea to institutes, study sections and NOSIs via RePORTER, matches mechanisms with mechanism_matcher.py and writes a .docx strategy. NIH only.

entries.name: litreview
entries.description: Use when starting a literature review or a literature-based project. Plans the search (PICO, SPIDER) with framework_recommender.py, searches PubMed and OpenAlex with free_search.py and writes a .docx orientation guide. Single-paper lookups: query directly.

entries.name: meta-research
entries.description: Use when a wrong answer is expensive: strategy research, comparing several products or markets, validating a hypothesis with outside data. Fans out searches and sub-agents, triangulates each claim across 3+ sources and saves every source with quotes. Quick facts: answer directly.

entries.name: notebooklm
entries.description: Use for anything in Google NotebookLM: querying notebooks, adding sources, generating Audio or Video Overviews, reports, flashcards or slides. Drives the browser; needs browser automation.

entries.name: patent
entries.description: Use for prior-art search, freedom-to-operate, patent landscape, acquisition diligence or litigation prior art. Picks the use case with sub_use_case_router.py, searches Google Patents, Espacenet and USPTO and writes a .docx; not legal advice.

entries.name: pulse
entries.description: Use for what people are saying right now about a topic (trends, sentiment, complaints, tool comparisons) across Reddit, Hacker News and the web in a recent window. Returns a cited briefing with engagement signals.

entries.name: research
entries.description: Use for any research request that doesn't clearly match a research specialist ('research X', 'look into Y'). Routes with classifier.py to pulse, grants, litreview, syllabus, patent, dossier or deepread, or runs its own cited search.

entries.name: syllabus
entries.description: Use when the user shares a course syllabus or outline and wants supplementary readings. Groups topics with topic_grouper.py, finds recent peer-reviewed papers and writes a .docx with summaries and discussion questions.
